author: Alex Berger
title: East Greenbush residents share concerns for potential Flock cameras - NewsBreak
text:
By Alex Berger ,
1 hours ago
EAST GREENBUSH, N.Y. ( NEWS10 ) — It was hazy outside in East Greenbush on Wednesday, but in Town Hall, the message was clear from many residents who had concerns regarding the town board considering Flock Safety cameras.
Download our WTEN+ streaming app on Roku, Fire TV and Apple TV! “Nobody came to support flock cameras.” That was the observation Jack Conway, town supervisor of East Greenbush, said aloud following a presentation from Flock Safety representatives to the town board.
Several residents in attendance at Wednesday night’s board meeting voiced their opposition to potentially having these cameras up in their town.
Flock cameras are motion-activated license plate readers, that according to the company, are intended to track down stolen vehicles and deter crime.
No cameras have been put up in East Greenbush, but the town board is weighing whether or not they should have a contract with the Georgia-based technology company.
“Our mission at the end of the day is to support communities like East Greenbush, who we believe as we have the right to thrive from a public safety perspective with our mission being to eliminate crime,” said Joe DiStefano.
Get the latest news, weather, sports and entertainment delivered right to your inbox! Flock cameras are already set up in many towns across the country, including Troy .
One resident expressed concern during Wednesday night’s meeting that drivers aren’t giving Flock their consent to be tracked.
A representative from the East Greenbush Police Department responded to the resident by saying she gives consent to be tracked “when you register your vehicle.”
Residents are also concerned that this technology, and their information, could fall into the wrong hands.
“We’ve hired third parties to try to hack us to identify vulnerabilities,” said Karl Bach, a representative for Flock. “It’s an ongoing challenge. We’re never going to be 100% certain that we cannot be, but we have not been breached or hacked.”
That explanation did not cut it for some citizens.
“The safety measures story doesn’t track,” said one resident.
A public forum to continue this conversation regarding Flock cameras will be held on September 16 at Town Hall.
Conway told residents who would want to file a Freedom of Information Law request regarding Flock that he would waive the fees attached to those requests.
